verdicts.reason: In all 313 specs the owningProof is the retired file itself, so no proof is named, which L12-129 requires. 53 specs have empty reasonTargets: they read no moved record and are retired only because they enumerate, which is scope beyond the size goal and saves 3.3 MB in total. Ten are current Phase 09 gate replayers (census-join/join.py, composition/*, preserve-premise/*, carries/*). They are conditioned, but the measured tip already assumes them gone.

The 10 files are pass/fail-identical (292/295 each side, same 3 titles, no ENOENT after reduction; verified). But both ownership tests fail at audit-ownership before checks.mjs, so the reduction's effect on check A is never observed. Statically, checks.mjs lines 9/23 put every non-merge first-parent commit since B0 into offender pairs, and 375 of the 573 moved paths are outside allowed-paths.json. The removal commit therefore adds unaccounted A pairs. The design must name pair accounting for the archive commit, or land the removal so check A excludes it.

A reviewer rebuild (pin tree − 573 records + 16 included artifacts at c9826a369) gives 16,243 files / 1,269,268,475 B against the claimed 16,243 / 1,269,268,322. The 153 B difference is the disclosed post-measurement wording edit. Plan share is 1,085,588,864 B; non-plan tip is 183.7 MB.

Only part of the retained bytes is justified. 47 files ≥1 MB (491 MB) have live-reader reasons: identity registries 170 MB, Phase 02 inventory parts 195 MB, ledger shards, rationale inputs. But 5,663 files / 540 MB are kept only by the inherited 1 MB threshold, with no reader reason, and that is the largest single block. The design says reaching 0.2 GB needs 'retirement/repoint of still-live inventory inputs', which misstates the cause. Its reasons also mislabel live product inputs (claim-and-disposition-vocabulary.json, alias-table.json, shipped-path-conventions-inventory.json, step-06-evidence-consumer-table.json, dropped-claims-register.json, claim-ledger.schema.json, plan.md) as just 'small record', so they cannot guide a next cut.
